To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of natural phosphate as catalyst support is a promising alternative to conventional supports; 2) it is possible to control the surface composition and structure of the resulting platinum catalyst and to relate it to catalytic performance; 3) it is possible, by means of a post-synthesis treatment, to modify the surface structure of the most active catalyst and to obtain a catalyst with improved selectivity to crolyl alcohol.

1) natural phosphates can be used as support for platinum; 2) the most active systems show new surface interactions; 3) further modification of the most promising system leads to high selectivity to crolyl alcohol at high conversion.
